rules.title: Secrets key Decrypt by an unexpected principal

model.expression:
fields coalesce(detail.userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn, detail.userIdentity.arn, "unknown") as principal
| filter principal not like /^arn:aws:iam::${SECRETS_DECRYPTS_LOG_GROUP_ACCOUNT_ID}:role\/boxel-(realm-server|worker)-${SECRETS_DECRYPTS_ENV}-ecs-task$/ or ispresent(detail.errorCode)
| stats count() as unexpected by bin(5m)

annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}Something other than this environment's realm-server or worker task role, in this account, called kms:Decrypt on the secrets key, or a Decrypt on it was denied, in the last 30 minutes (CloudTrail, copied by EventBridge into the decrypts log group). The window covers CloudTrail's delivery delay. Read the record on the Keys dashboard or in the log group: the principal, source IP and encryption context. A task role's Decrypt that is not at a task's startup is a shell opened in the task: look up ExecuteCommand in CloudTrail. See the secrets-at-rest skill's audit.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about who called Decrypt on the secrets key. The query reads CloudWatch: the Error annotation's text says why, usually throttling or a missing permission.{{ end }}

rules.title: Many keys rejected at one host

model.expr: max(count by (host) (sum by (host, key) (count_over_time({service=~"realm-server|worker"} |= "boxel:key-grant" | json | drop __error__, __error_details__ | line_format `{{ if .log }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " .log "" }}{{ else }}{{ regexReplaceAll "^\\[worker [^\\]]+\\]: " __line__ "" }}{{ end }}` | json | channel="boxel:key-grant" | event=~"grant-rejected|key-rejected" [10m]))))

annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}Grants or keys of three or more distinct keys at one destination host entered the rejected state in the last 10 minutes. Keys are counted, not grants: one key can hold several grants at one host (one per destination path), so one revoked key rejects them all and counts once. Three keys refused at one host at once is that vendor refusing every key (an outage, or a change to its auth) or a substitution bug of ours sending the wrong value. Check the vendor's status page, then whether keys at other hosts still work. Probes return the grants to active on their own once the vendor accepts them again. See the key-outage-triage skill.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about keys or vendors. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}
